subject: START statement
notes: kb/Work PB236 (landed). RULE (cite.py --check 14.9.41.4 OK, GR8): 'If the KEY phrase is omitted, the START statement behaves as though KEY IS EQUAL TO data-name-1 had been specified, where data-name-1 is the name of the key specified in the RELATIVE KEY clause associated with file-name-1.' MAIN PATH -- VERIFIED and unchanged: BindStart defaults the operator to '==' and the operand to file.RelativeKeyItem, which is exactly GR8's substitution and is consistent with GR10 (observed on probe/rel-start/STPRB1 step A: RRN 2/4/6 written, MOVE 4 TO RK, bare START RELFA takes NOT INVALID KEY with FS='00' and READ NEXT returns REC-4). THE EDGE IS NOW CLOSED, which is what moved this row. A relative file in ACCESS SEQUENTIAL may omit the RELATIVE KEY clause -- 12.4.5.13 imposes no requirement to write it and the compiler requires it only for random/dynamic access -- so the source is LEGAL and GR8's substitution has no operand: there is no data-name-1 to compare and the standard gives the statement no meaning. It used to compile clean and abort the run unit with NotImplementedCobolFeatureException. It is now rejected at bind, in the SAME COBOL0862 channel this method already uses for SR1/SR3/SR5/SR6/SR8, so the asymmetry that had two of START's five refusals carrying a diagnostic and three not is gone. Measured: `error COBOL0862: START on 'RNK': the KEY phrase is omitted, so ISO 14.9.41.4 GR8 substitutes KEY IS EQUAL TO the RELATIVE KEY item -- but this file control entry has no RELATIVE KEY clause, so there is no key to compare.` The licence to flag is explicit: cite.py --check 4.2.2 'An implementation may, but is not required to, flag violations of such rules.' -> OK -- and the alternative to flagging is emitting code that cannot work. Witness: conformance:cases/14.9.41-START/pb236-start-relative-no-relative-key.
